draft.title: How the Mongols conquered
card: Mongol armies were made up of mounted archers. Each soldier rode a horse and could shoot a bow accurately while riding.
Soldiers often had several spare horses, so an army could travel far each day. This speed let it surprise enemies who thought they had time to prepare.
Mongol commanders used clever tactics. One was a fake retreat: the army pretended to flee, then turned on enemies who chased it and broke their formation.

The Mongols also used terror. Cities that gave up quickly were often spared, but cities that resisted could be destroyed. News of this made others more likely to surrender. Using these methods, the Mongols built the largest land empire in history.
draft.remember: Speed, tactics and terror together made Mongol armies hard to stop.

a.q: Why could a Mongol army reach enemies faster than most armies of its time?
opts: Soldiers rode horses and brought spare ones
Soldiers wore heavy armour that protected them
Soldiers sailed along rivers in large fleets
Soldiers marched in huge groups along set roads
a.why: Riding with spare horses meant the army could cover long distances each day. Heavy armour would have slowed the riders, so it does not explain their speed.
a.clue: Think about how the soldiers travelled and what they brought with them.

b.q: A Mongol army pretends to flee. The enemy chases it and falls into disorder, and the Mongols turn and attack. What does this show?
opts: A clever tactic that used the enemy's own eagerness
The use of terror to make a city surrender
A lack of discipline among the Mongol soldiers
The use of spare horses to reach a city quickly
b.why: The fake retreat is a tactic that tricked the enemy into breaking formation. Terror is a different method: it relied on the fear caused by destroying cities that resisted, not on a trick in battle.
b.clue: Was the enemy tricked in battle, or frightened by news of destruction?

a.best: Soldiers rode horses and brought spare ones

b.best: A clever tactic that used the enemy's own eagerness

problems.detail: The clue 'what they brought with them' points straight at the only option that mentions bringing something ('brought spare ones'), so a student can pick it without knowing the idea.
